schedules.title: Memory curation
schedules.description: Keeps your second brain tidy: files durable learnings from recent chats, applies accepted memory proposals, and updates project notes when something changed. Reports only what it processed; does nothing on a quiet day.
schedules.prompt: Curate recent archived chats, memory proposals, and durable learnings. Use the memory agent. Prefer existing session-insights sections and update the configured vault; append durable learnings to `Workspace/Learnings.md` (error resolutions, non-obvious workarounds, user corrections, outdated assumptions, not routine work). Promote durable cross-session facts into the bounded memory regions of the workspace `CLAUDE.md`: the `ciao:memory` region for cross-project preferences, environment facts, and lessons learned, and the `ciao:profile` region for user identity and communication style. Both regions are already in your system prompt, and each section header carries its current usage, so read the header. There is no memory command; edit the regions with `Edit`. Remove entries whose valid `[expires: YYYY-MM-DD]` date has passed, and report malformed expiration tags instead of guessing. When a region is at or above ~85% of its cap, consolidate BEFORE promoting: merge related entries and remove stale one-off corrections that have no reuse value (e.g. "User said X -> assistant did Y" single-doc edits, resolved open loops), so there is headroom. Nothing enforces the cap at write time, so the cap is your responsibility. Then run `ciao memory-audit --json` and act on the rot it reports, because the regions load on every single turn and a wrong claim there is asserted before the user has said a word. Every fact is either state (a current value, which you REPLACE when it changes) or an event (a thing that happened, which you APPEND to a log and never edit). For each `event_shaped_entries` finding, move that entry out of the region and into `Workspace/Learnings.md`: it records a chat turn, not a current value. For each `stale_path_entries` finding, open the cited path, then correct it or drop the claim; do not assume the finding is right, since a path can be missing here and correct in a sibling repo. Treat `superseded_state_candidates` as a question rather than a defect: when one entry supersedes another, keep only the current value, and when the two describe different facets of the subject, leave both. Report the counts you fixed and the ones you deliberately kept. If `ciao memory-audit` is unavailable or fails, say so plainly and continue; never report the surface as clean on the strength of a command that did not run. Then review pending batches in `Workspace/Memory-Proposals.md`. Route each fact by scope: put a fact in a memory region ONLY when it applies across projects. A fact scoped to one project belongs in that project's canonical doc. Standing operating directives belong in the `CLAUDE.md` body OUTSIDE the fenced regions: the regions hold remembered facts, the body holds instructions. When consolidating, move any project-scoped entry sitting in a region out to its owning project doc rather than deleting it. Also skim the guide body: if it holds remembered facts rather than standing directives, move them into the memory region. Leave genuine directives in place, and when unsure whether something is a fact or a directive, propose the move rather than editing the body. Remove processed batches from the proposals file, editing the region first and dismissing the proposal second so a failed turn cannot lose the fact. Never skip a durable fact because a region is full; consolidate to make room instead. Scan recently archived chats by project: when session-insights contain Decisions, Open loops, or material status changes for a vault-backed project, update that project's canonical doc and `log.md` if present, only when something actually changed. If nothing new needs processing, reply with a one-line no-op and stop. Report only processed counts plus changed files.

schedules.title: Workspace hygiene
schedules.description: Weekly AI OS health check: rebuilds the vault index, repairs safe link drift, and audits knowledge, skills, instructions, bounded memory, and unresolved automation failures.
schedules.prompt: Run a complete AI OS hygiene pass. Complete all five steps in one go, and summarize command output instead of pasting raw JSON or index content. Steps: 1) Run `ciao vault-index --write` to regenerate memory-vault/INDEX.md. The `--write` flag is required. If vault-index fails, report the failure, skip link or index repairs, and do not claim the workspace is healthy or return a no-op. 2) Run `ciao os-audit --json`. Exit code 1 means the audit ran successfully and found items needing attention; continue the routine. Exit code 2 means the audit could not inspect required evidence reliably; report its scan errors and do not claim the workspace is healthy. 3) When the index rebuild and audit are reliable, apply only low-risk, unambiguous fixes: repair or remove dead wikilinks and fix obvious MEMORY.md drift where index entries point at files that moved or no longer exist. Do not automatically rewrite instruction conflicts, skills, orphaned notes, duplicates, invalid expiration tags, or schedule prompts. 4) After any fixes, run `ciao os-audit --json` again to verify the remaining findings. 5) Report initial and final issue counts, what was fixed, unresolved findings, and scan errors. If the first reliable audit is healthy, reply with a one-line no-op and stop.

schedules.title: Skill evolution
schedules.description: Weekly look at how your custom skills performed: reviews recent sessions for errors and corrections and drafts improvement proposals for skills that struggled. Proposals are saved for your review — nothing is applied automatically, and it does nothing if you have no custom skills.
schedules.prompt: Run `python3 -m ciao.skill_evolution` with the workspace default model. Summarize proposals written and any failed gates. Do not apply proposals automatically.
